items.title: Lured by High Salaries, Some Brazilians Were Duped Into Fighting for Russia
items.excerpt: Dozens of Brazilians were sent to the front lines with little training, and the high salaries they were promised, they say, turned out to be illusory.

items.title: After Cyberattacks and Bomb Threats Hit Europe, Survivalism Goes Mainstream
items.excerpt: More governments in Europe are telling citizens to prepare for emergencies. After unexpected disruptions, many are listening.

items.title: Net Migration to U.K. Falls to Lowest Level Since 1997, Excluding Pandemic
items.excerpt: The drop was largely driven by fewer people arriving from outside the European Union. It reflects government action to restrict immigration after a public backlash.

items.title: U.K. Releases Files on Peter Mandelson, Ambassador Tied to Jeffrey Epstein
items.excerpt: Documents released Thursday shed new light on the rushed appointment of Peter Mandelson and his continued ties to Global Counsel, a lobbying group.

items.title: Two Italians Killed in Iranian Drone Attack on Kuwait, Officials Say
items.excerpt: The deaths follow a series of strikes on Gulf Arab states that host U.S. military facilities in recent weeks as talks to end the war continue to stall.

items.title: Gérard Depardieu Is Ordered to Stand Trial Over Rape Accusation
items.excerpt: The actress Charlotte Arnould has accused the French movie star of raping her in 2018. He has denied any wrongdoing in the case.

items.title: El Salvador’s Nayib Bukele Elates Haiti With Fight Against Gangs
items.excerpt: The president of El Salvador has widespread support among Haitians, who are tired of violence and hope he can be the one to finally end it.

items.title: Brazilian Duped Into Fighting for Russia: ‘War Is Hell’
items.excerpt: Dozens of Brazilians have joined the Russian army, some say lured by a pair of recruiters promising money and adventure. Here is one soldier’s story.

items.title: Hong Kong Grieves Fire Victims Under Watchful Eye of Authorities
items.excerpt: The city’s residents quietly mourned the 168 lives lost in a high-rise complex blaze a year ago, as officials warned against using the disaster to sow division.

items.title: The Unbearable Heat of Delhi’s Summer Nights
items.excerpt: Residents of India’s dense capital tried switching off fridges and leaving doors open all night to cope with rising temperatures, which affect their sleep, health and ability to work.

items.title: Attack Blamed on ISIS Kills 2 Syrian Security Force Members
items.excerpt: The assault on a security headquarters in the northeastern city of Hasakah was carried out by four militants who local officials linked to the Islamic State.

items.title: An Italian Couple Bought a House Built by Pier Paolo Pasolini. Local Villagers Want to Evict Them.
items.excerpt: After an Italian couple bought a house built by Pier Paolo Pasolini, one of the country’s greatest film directors, local villagers claimed the property.

items.title: Was Japan Prime Minister Takaichi Snubbed at China’s Big Summit?
items.excerpt: Images show the differences between the welcomes afforded to Sanae Takaichi and other world leaders in Shenzhen, as some officials in Japan cry foul.

items.title: Island Paradise of Mauritius Has Sun, Beaches and Too Many Dogs
items.excerpt: Mauritius, a popular tourist destination off southern Africa, has become overrun with strays. With more and more residents chased and attacked, many are fed up.

items.title: Ontario Premier Says He’d Use a Gun to Protect His Family
items.excerpt: Recent home invasions have stirred unease in Toronto. On Thursday, the premier of Ontario said he would fire a gun in self-defense ‘in a heartbeat.’

items.title: In Praise of My Typewriter
items.excerpt: The A.I. projects editor at The New York Times uses chatbots every day. But when it’s time to write, he reaches for an Olivetti Lettera 22 from the 1950s.

items.title: The E.R. Closed at 5 P.M. A Dying Woman Showed Up 11 Minutes Too Late.
items.excerpt: In rural British Columbia, Courtney McCowan died after paramedics tried to help her in a hospital’s parking lot.

items.title: How Birds With GPS and Audio Sensors Track Hidden Fishing Boats
items.excerpt: Researchers are using seabirds equipped with GPS and audio gear to detect vessels that operate with no tracking signals and to assess the environmental hazards they pose.

items.title: London Banning Noise and Capping Fares for Its Pedicabs
items.excerpt: Starting Friday, the city will regulate pedicab operators for the first time, imposing fare caps and noise restrictions.

items.title: Can Roof Tiles Reduce Indoor Heat? India Is Finding Out.
items.excerpt: As temperatures soar, researchers are experimenting with ways to make life more comfortable for the most vulnerable.

items.title: Africa C.D.C. Chief Faces Turmoil Over Management Amid Ebola Crisis
items.excerpt: Scrutiny has fallen on Dr. Jean Kaseya, the director general of the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, after reports of staff intimidation and mismanagement of funds.

items.title: Gordon Ramsay to Host Revival of BBC’s ‘Top Gear’
items.excerpt: The British car show “Top Gear” paused production three years ago and is returning with a new host in 2028, the BBC said.

items.title: Road Fire Near Cairo Kills Dozens After Petroleum-Laden Truck Crashes
items.excerpt: The blaze killed at least 31 and injured at least 21 near Giza, beside the Nile River, officials said.

items.title: Study Hard, Get Ahead?
items.excerpt: The broken promise of upward mobility through education is sparking youth protests around the world.

items.title: Judges in Israel Suggest Dropping Key Corruption Case Against Netanyahu
items.excerpt: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is accused of bribery, fraud and breach of trust in a long-running trial that has divided the country. He denies all wrongdoing.

items.title: Lukoil to Sell Foreign Assets, but Not to Kushner and Witkoff Associates
items.excerpt: Valuable properties belonging to the Russian energy giant will be sold to an American-led consortium. But Middle Eastern business contacts of the two Trump envoys pulled out because of political winds.

items.title: Opposition Makes Progress Toward Ousting Netanyahu, Party Leader Says
items.excerpt: Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief, has set Dec. 6 as the deadline to form a new Israeli government. His ally, Avigdor Liberman, said Mr. Eisenkot was on track.

items.title: South African President Wins Reprieve From ‘Farmgate’ Impeachment Investigation
items.excerpt: A court threw out a report suggesting that Cyril Ramaphosa may have tried to conceal the theft of more than half a million dollars of U.S. currency.

items.title: How to Celebrate Thanksgiving as an Expat
items.excerpt: From turkeys delivered on motorbikes to foie gras on the table, many American expatriates have adapted the traditional meal to their environs.

items.title: Libyan Forces Threaten Retaliation Over Ukraine’s Attack on Russian Ships
items.excerpt: The Ukrainian drone strike off Libya’s coast killed two Libyan naval officers, according to the forces controlling the country’s east.
